name: Pancam Mast Assembly (PMA)
desc: Elevates stereo Pancam and Navcam sensors 1.5 meters above the ground, replicating human eye height. Incorporates 360° azimuthal pan and ±90° elevation gimbals with 16 narrow-band multispectral filters.

discoveryLink.scienceFinding: Identified the fine layered sedimentary lamination in Eagle Crater cliff walls and pinpointed hematite spherule beds.
discoveryLink.significance: Proved that sediment was deposited in a body of flowing or undulating liquid water rather than volcanic ash alone.

name: GaAs Solar Array Wings
desc: 1.3 m² triple-junction Gallium Arsenide (GaAs/Ge) photovoltaic cells generating 140 W at landing, degrading to ~100 W under atmospheric dust. Cleaned repeatedly by unexpected Martian aeolian cleaning events.

discoveryLink.scienceFinding: Direct measurement of atmospheric optical depth (tau) and discovery of Martian 'cleaning events' caused by wind vortexes.
discoveryLink.significance: Demonstrated that Martian weather could periodically clean solar panels, enabling mission lifespan to extend from 90 sols to 15 years.

name: Rocker-Bogie Mobility System
desc: Six independently motorized 26-cm diameter aluminum cleated wheels linked via differential rocker-bogie linkages without springs. Allows scaling obstacles larger than wheel diameter (25 cm) with chassis tilt limited to ±25°.

discoveryLink.scienceFinding: When Opportunity's right-front steering actuator jammed in 2005, engineers drove the rover backwards. The jammed wheel trench-dragged up pure bright silica deposits.
discoveryLink.significance: Uncovered hydrothermal vent deposits, indicating ancient volcanic fumaroles or hot springs ideal for micro-organic habitats.

name: Instrument Deployment Device (IDD)
desc: 5-degree-of-freedom robotic manipulator carrying a 4-instrument turret: Mössbauer Spectrometer (MIMOS II), Alpha Particle X-Ray Spectrometer (APXS), Microscopic Imager (MI), and Rock Abrasion Tool (RAT).

discoveryLink.scienceFinding: The RAT ground away 5mm of weathered rock patina from the 'El Capitan' outcrop, allowing the APXS to detect high concentrations of sulfur and jarosite.
discoveryLink.significance: Provided indisputable chemical fingerprinting that acidic liquid water soaked the Martian surface in its formative geological era.

name: High-Gain Steerable Dish (HGA)
desc: 0.28-meter parabolic reflector dish steerable in azimuth and elevation to beam telemetry directly to Earth's Deep Space Network (DSN) via X-Band (8.4 GHz) at bitrates between 3.5 kbps and 128 kbps.

discoveryLink.scienceFinding: Ultra-precise Doppler shift tracking of the HGA radio carrier wave as Mars rotated.
discoveryLink.significance: Allowed planetary geophysicists to measure Mars' core precession, confirming the planet possesses a liquid outer iron core.

name: RAD6000 Warm Electronics Box (WEB)
desc: Centrally mounted insulated compartment housing the BAE RAD6000 20 MHz 32-bit RISC processor, 128 MB RAM, and dual 8 Ah Li-ion batteries. Kept warm by aerogel insulation and 8 Radioisotope Heater Units (RHUs).

discoveryLink.scienceFinding: The RAD6000 computed real-time stereo disparity maps from Navcams, allowing Opportunity to autonomously navigate around treacherous sand ripples without Earth intervention.
discoveryLink.significance: Pioneered planetary rover autonomous traverse, enabling Opportunity to drive hundreds of meters across uncharted extraterrestrial landscapes per Sol.
